sections.heading: Introduction and Goals
sections.text:
UtterPlan is the canonical, engine-independent semantic compiler from one SSMD 0.9
document (or explicitly selected plain-text document) to an executable speech plan.
It owns document parsing, language runs, source linguistic analysis, SSMD annotation
meanings, coordinate mapping, spoken-text analysis, segmentation, canonical boundary
opportunities, authored pause intent, directives, and FlowPlan construction. It uses
TTSReady for reusable written-to-spoken preparation and stops before G2P, synthesis,
and audio.

sections.heading: Quality goals
sections.text:
Goal

Motivation





Deterministic, renderer-independent plans

The same source and configuration always produce the same executable plan and plan_id, so consumers can cache, compare, and verify plans safely.



Safe boundaries and authored pauses stay separate

Downstream renderers keep full freedom for chunking and pause realization without changing plan semantics.



Portable, file-roundtrippable persistence

.utterplan.toml is the single interchange format; no semantic state exists outside serialized data.



Engine independence

Core code never imports synthesis engines, G2P packages, model runtimes, or audio libraries.



Sequential data-only migration

Every supported older schema has an explicit, deterministic path to the current contract.

sections.heading: Pause and directive semantics
sections.text:
Authored SSMD breaks project to local PauseIntent values on segment edges, while
safe clause, sentence, paragraph, parenthetical, and voice-change opportunities are
carried separately as boundary kinds. Both facts may coexist at one edge. UtterPlan
does not activate automatic pauses or invent numeric durations; downstream
renderers choose native, automatic, or manual realization. Exact authored timed
breaks remain exact. Ambiguous historical pause evidence fails migration rather
than being guessed.

Typed directives are renderer-neutral values resolved from SSMD scopes and voice
defaults. Logical voice bindings remain references, not concrete engine voices.
Audio references and extension names are data only; UtterPlan does not fetch media
or execute handlers.

sections.heading: Identity and determinism
sections.text:
Plan identity is deterministic and renderer-independent. The v7 plan_id includes
the exact UTF-8 SHA-256 digest of optional raw source, plus executable flow,
canonical boundary opportunities, authored pause intents, and compact portable
metadata; it never hashes TOML formatting. The v7 utterplan-flow-v3 identity
includes boundaries, while v5/v6 retain their historical hash schemas. Renderer
chunk and pause strategies are not identity inputs. Trace data, provider documents,
model sessions, diagnostics, producer/package version, G2P output, and audio do not
define executable identity. Package version is independent of explicit plan
schema_version.

sections.heading: Preparation and source retention
sections.text:
Preparation creates structural and spoken representations internally. The
executable FlowPlan retains prepared segment text and compact segment-local
replacement views, and v7 stores the exact raw input once in its optional
PlanSource record; it does not retain structural text or full source-to-spoken
maps, parser annotations, or global compiler token tables. Detailed diagnostics and
complete provenance mappings remain in an optional trace.

sections.heading: Persistence and atomic IO
sections.text:
Plans persist as deterministic .utterplan.toml files. Writes use atomic IO
(temporary file plus replace) so interrupted operations never leave partial plan
files; the same mechanism protects batch reports and book outputs.

sections.heading: Renderability policy
sections.text:
Safe punctuation-only repair is the default; --renderability strict rejects every
repair opportunity. Neither mode guesses a symbol’s pronunciation or crosses
semantic blockers. Blocked planning outcomes may be reviewed through the separate
utterplan.planning-attempt.v1 inspect-only artifact; such candidates remain
drafts and never become canonical plans.

sections.heading: Manifest-driven SSMD bundles
sections.text:
UtterPlan’s bundle lifecycle accepts one canonical <name>.ssmd-bundle/ root and dispatches from its manifest.json. Both compilation and projection use this entry point:

utterplan bundle compile novel.ssmd-bundle --chapters 5-17
utterplan bundle compile story.ssmd-bundle
utterplan bundle render novel.ssmd-bundle --chapters 5-17 --profile narration.renderprofile.toml
utterplan bundle render story.ssmd-bundle --profile narration.renderprofile.toml




The manifest format determines whether the bundle contains independently planned book items or one document item. A chapter directory, document source file, or arbitrary directory is not an alternate root. UtterPlan reads manifests and source documents but does not modify them.

sections.heading: Manifest kinds
sections.text:
Both supported manifests use schema_version: 1 and ssmd_version: "0.9".

A book manifest declares format: "ssmdconvert.book" and a chapters array. Every chapter has a unique id, positive source_number, title, and normalized relative POSIX path; optional hashes are informational and do not override the current source content. Chapter paths are resolved within the bundle root.

A document manifest declares format: "ssmdconvert.document" and one document object containing an id, relative path, and document metadata. Its current source is compiled as one FlowPlan. The bundle’s name does not select its kind: manifest.json is authoritative.

sections.heading: Directives and media
sections.text:
Voice bindings and directive voice references are logical names, not backend voice IDs; consumers translate them to engine-specific resources. UtterPlan resolves SSMD scopes and defaults but does not choose engine settings or realize downstream pause policy; consumers interpret saved boundary and authored-pause facts.

An audio directive is already attached to its owning segment. Its src is opaque data for an external resolver; UtterPlan does not select or invoke one. For an audio-bearing segment, segment.text is an optional spoken fallback. Identical source URIs on distinct segments are separate timeline occurrences and must not be deduplicated as playback events. Extension references are also data only; UtterPlan does not execute handlers.

sections.heading: PyKokoro integration boundary
sections.text:
UtterPlan is an independent planning compiler. PyKokoro is an optional consumer, not a runtime dependency of this package. A thin adapter can preserve the existing PyKokoro user API:

KokoroPipeline.run(text)
    -> map PipelineConfig and GenerationConfig to PlannerConfig
    -> UtterancePlanner.plan(text)
    -> adapt public FlowPlan segments to PyKokoro's G2P input
    -> PyKokoro G2P
    -> phoneme processing
    -> model inference
    -> audio




PyKokoro owns model selection, voice assets, G2P, model tokens, ONNX sessions, acoustic behavior, and audio. UtterPlan owns deterministic document parsing, language planning, written-to-spoken preparation, canonical segmentation, safe boundary opportunities, authored pause intents, typed directives, markers, and paragraph-local flow units.

sections.heading: TOML persistence
sections.text:
Schema v7 is the current semantic contract, while .utterplan.toml is the canonical persisted format. FlowPlan.to_toml() and FlowPlan.from_toml() round-trip the current executable plan; save() writes atomically, and load() accepts TOML only. All normal decode/load and execution paths reject non-v7 plans with schema.version_unsupported; they never migrate implicitly. sections.heading: Unified bundle services
sections.text:
compile_bundle(), render_bundle(), and replan_bundle() are the public Python counterparts of utterplan bundle compile|render|replan. They accept a canonical <name>.ssmd-bundle/ path and dispatch book or document behavior from its manifest. The CLI delegates to these services, so selection and path-safety rules are shared.

sections.text:
UtterancePlanner.plan, UtterancePlanner.compile, and compile_document accept an optional keyword-only on_progress callback. sections.heading: SSMD input and semantic plan
sections.text:
The SSMD parser accepts dialect 0.9 only. Select SSMD explicitly for unversioned canonical fragments with PlannerConfig(document_format="ssmd"). Older SSMD source must be migrated with ssmd migrate FILE --to 0.9; migrate_plan_data operates on serialized plan mappings, while utterplan migrate imports legacy plans, not source documents.

PlannerConfig.document_format defaults to "plain", so SSMD syntax is never inferred for an ordinary Python string. Set it to "ssmd" for SSMD documents or fragments. There is no compile-time pause activation setting: authored SSMD breaks are represented as PauseIntent, while automatic safe boundaries remain separate boundary_before / boundary_after values. Consumers choose how to realize either fact without changing plan identity.

sections.heading: Flow segments and local tokens
Audio/media segments
sections.text:
AudioDirective is already part of the public API. Inspect it on the segment; its
src is an opaque renderer input, and segment.text is optional spoken fallback:

segment = plan.flow[0].segments[0]
audio = segment.directives.audio
if audio is not None:
    print(audio.src)  # Resolve externally; do not parse SFX URI syntax here.
    fallback_text = segment.text  # May be "" when no spoken fallback exists.
else:
    spoken_text = segment.text




Each SSMD audio annotation is represented by one audio-bearing segment. Separate
occurrences may have the same src; segment.text is not the media identity and
consumers do not need to inspect raw SSMD annotations to find media.

sections.heading: Errors
sections.text:
Planning and loading failures derive from utterplan.UtterPlanError. Important
public subclasses include ConfigurationError, PlanningError,
PlanFormatError, PlanValidationError, and UnsupportedSchemaError.
PlanMigrationError and MigrationPathError report migration-specific failures. UnsupportedSchemaError remains reserved for a schema newer than the installed package understands.

PlanRenderabilityError presents the same actionable source and spoken context as the CLI, including safe repair opportunities, semantic blockers, and a next action. Safe punctuation-only repair is the default; choose PlannerConfig(renderability_mode="strict") when a caller needs to reject every repair opportunity. Symbols are never assigned guessed pronunciations.
